Screenshot of a Bluesky post in dark mode, with a dark navy background and white text.

At the top, three profile badges read: “AI Hater” (bearded man emoji), “Posts over 20 times per day on average” (yellow broadcast emoji), and “Joined Aug ’23” (blue globe emoji). A fourth badge on the next line reads “Bluesky Elder” (elderly person emoji).

The post reads:

“You got this all backwards. Users are creating and curating free content to fill your shell of a website.

You’re welcome.”

Below the post are Bluesky’s interaction icons: reply, repost (2), like (229), bookmark, share, and more options.
A surprisingly delicious banh mi with a bite taken out of it

Scatter plot titled "Agents' Last Exam v1.1" on a black background, plotting Score (vertical axis from 60% to 80%) against Cost (horizontal axis from $0 to $60). The legend lists models represented by different colored stars, suns, squares, and triangles: GPT-6.2 Astra (blue star), GPT-6.2 Sol (yellow sun), Claude Fable 5.2 (dark grey square), Gemini 4 Carbon (light grey triangle), GPT-6 Astra (blue star), GPT-6.1 Sol (yellow sun), and Claude Opus 5.5 (grey plus sign). Multiple data points are clustered near the low-cost end ($0) reaching higher scores, with a few other data points scattered at higher costs.

A line graph titled "Length of coding and ML research tasks that different AI models can complete 80% of the time". The y-axis measures "Task duration (for humans)" from 0 to 48 hours, and the x-axis shows "Release date" from 2020 to 2027. The chart features three trendlines showing exponential growth: a 2019–2025 trend doubling every 7 months (teal), a 2024–early 2026 trend doubling every 3.3 months (yellow dashed), and a steep trend since Opus 4.5 doubling every 1.7 months (maroon). Key data points include GPT-2, GPT-3, GPT-3.5, GPT-4, Claude Mythos Preview (measured at 3.1 hours in early 2026), and an estimated "~38 hours" for "Model 4" (Anthropic internal).

I conflated people skeptical of Al doom with people who understand the technical alignment problem, have credible forecasting records, and nevertheless expect us to retain control of
superintelligence. Those are very different groups.
screenshot of the quoted post embedded on a feed called "what else is like this"

A block diagram titled "NVIDIA GPUs" on the left and "Quantum QPU" on the right, connected by bidirectional arrows labeled "NVQLink + CUDA-Q" below. The left box lists "Error correction", "Calibration + control", and "Circuit simulation". The right box lists "Physical qubits", "Quantum operations", and "Measurement".

Why Both Sides Talk Past Each Other

If you look at total cumulative emissions today, non-Al digital infrastructure-video streaming, enterprise cloud storage, social media, and traditional web hosting-still accounts for roughly three-quarters of all data center electricity and emissions. Attributing the entire 25.7 million tons in the Harvard study solely to Al

is factually inaccurate.

However, if you look at marginal emissions-

new power plants built because of load growth, Al is the primary driver. Traditional data center energy use stayed nearly flat between 2014 and 2017 because efficiency improvements matched demand growth. The sharp upward inflection since 2018-and the wave of behind-the-meter natural gas turbines and delayed coal retirements in states like Virginia, Louisiana, Ohio, and Texas-is overwhelmingly driven by high-density GPU campuses.
